blocks.text: When subject matter experts try to ship changes today, review quickly becomes a bottleneck that goes back-and-forth. They can’t run the app themselves, so they ask an engineer for a screenshot, spot something off, and ask for a fix. Each round of review takes time and adds busywork.

blocks.text: Now, Cloud Agents can check the change in isolated cloud sandboxes before the pull request reaches anyone. blocks.text: What this means is that a feature request can now arrive as a tested pull request. Anyone can describe the change, close their laptop, and come back to a video of it working. Engineers get pull requests they don’t have to run themselves to understand, arriving in GitHub or GitLab already tested, with the video of the change working, ready to approve or provide feedback.

blocks.text: Broader workspace memory is a key function of Replit, and will be a key element of Self-Driving Companies. Internally at Replit, we’ve used it to reduce token usage by 51%, and cut the time agents take to complete a common data task from 16 minutes to 1 minute, without reducing output quality.

blocks.text: For many companies, code is one of the ground truths for how services work. There’s so much you can do with a full understanding of your product. With Replit, anyone in your company can now get answers grounded in what’s actually built. A support lead can find out why a customer keeps hitting an error. A product marketer can check that a feature works the way the launch copy says. A sales lead can see which team knows a feature best before proposing a change.

blocks.text: Set up the environment once, and everyone can contribute

inlines.text: Set up the environment once, and everyone can contribute

blocks.text: Getting a company’s app up and running takes the right repos, runtime versions, databases, background services, and credentials. Until now, every new contributor had to repeat that setup, a daunting task for a non-technical user. Deterred, they would build separately, or on outdated code, leaving engineers to reconcile the work, or creating a yawning gap between prototype and reality.

inlines.text: Getting a company’s app up and running takes the right repos, runtime versions, databases, background services, and credentials. Until now, every new contributor had to repeat that setup, a daunting task for a non-technical user. Deterred, they would build separately, or on outdated code, leaving engineers to reconcile the work, or creating a yawning gap between prototype and reality.

blocks.text: Replit has shared environments. An admin can set it up, and everyone can start from there. It just works. A Cloud Agent explores your codebase and configures an initial virtual machine (VM) that runs your app. The result is a ready-to-use environment with your repos, runtimes, skills, tools, and dependencies that anyone can use. It updates automatically from your main branch, so every new change starts from current code.

blocks.text: Contributors don’t see any of this. They just describe the change they want, and the agent starts from an app that’s already running. For engineers, environments handle what real apps need: dozens of programming languages, microservice architectures with several repos running together, Docker images, databases, queues, and caches. Credentials come from your external secrets managers through a credential broker.
